author: Joshua Fluke
description:
Companies really don't want employees asking about money.
One tech executive says he cut his sales team's guaranteed base salaries in half because, in his words, “if you're comfortable, you don't push.” Another recruiter says the best engineers aren't asking about salary first anymore — they're asking whether companies provide AI tools like Claude Code, Cursor and GitHub Copilot. And another recruiter questions a candidate because money is one of his primary motivations for accepting a paid job.

Apparently wanting to get paid is becoming a professional character flaw.
In this video, we're looking at salary, employee compensation, sales commission, job interviews, recruiters, tech jobs, AI coding tools, developer productivity, corporate culture and the increasingly strange ways companies try to convince workers that compensation shouldn't be their main concern.

title: COMPANIES REALLY DON'T WANT YOU ASKING ABOUT MONEY
